rubric.why: Distance is the total length of the path travelled.
rubric.description: Defines distance as the total length of the path travelled.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining distance as the total length of the path travelled.

rubric.why: Displacement is the straight-line change in position from the initial to the final position, with direction.
rubric.description: Defines displacement as the straight-line change in position, including direction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying displacement as a straight-line change in position and including its direction.

modelAnswer: Distance is the total length of the path travelled by a body.
Displacement is the shortest straight-line distance from the initial to the final position in a specified direction.

items.followUp: State the principle of moments and write its condition for equilibrium.

rubric.why: The principle applies to a body in equilibrium.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the body is in equilibrium.

rubric.why: For equilibrium, the sum of clockwise moments equals the sum of anticlockwise moments about the same pivot.
rubric.description: States the equality of clockwise and anticlockwise moments about the same pivot.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the clockwise and anticlockwise moments are equal about the same pivot.

modelAnswer: For a body in equilibrium, the sum of the clockwise moments about a pivot is equal to the sum of the anticlockwise moments about the same pivot.
